title: Trace Handoff Controller: OTLP bridge with smart sampling and backend mediation
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Background: Our hosted tracing pipeline needs a lightweight in-path controller that mediates OTLP span ingestion and performs dynamic sampling, header/tenant mapping, and backend-aware handoffs to both Jaeger and Tempo collectors. Existing components either duplicate logic or add latency; this ticket proposes a dedicated 'trace handoff controller' implemented as a stateless, horizontally-scalable service that sits between our ingestion gateway and backend exporters.

Goals: Build a bridge that (1) applies tenant-aware sampling policies configurable at runtime, (2) rewrites/normalizes trace attributes and headers for backend compatibility, (3) routes spans to Jaeger or Tempo (or both) based on policy and current backend health, and (4) maintains sub-ms processing overhead under expected peak throughput.

Scope: Implement the controller, a runtime config store for sampling rules (feature flags + simple rate maps), health/telemetry for backend selection, and integration tests with Jaeger collector (v1.30) and Tempo ingestion API. Provide a canary rollout path and dashboards for controller-level metrics (ingest rate, sampled rate, dropped spans, backend send latency, queue/backpressure).

Non-goals: Full trace enrichment (heavy attribute lookups), per-span redis-backed persistence, or replacing downstream long-term storage decisions. This work is focused on routing, sampling, and minimal normalization only.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Controller can accept OTLP/gRPC spans and forward to Jaeger and/or Tempo in our staging environment within 2% added p99 latency overhead compared to direct gateway->backend flow.
2) Sampling rules can be updated via runtime config without restarts and take effect within 30s.
3) Evidence of correct tenant mapping for at least 3 tenant formats (api-key header, x-tenant-id, and token-based mapping).
4) Automated e2e test that verifies failover to fallback backend when primary returns 5xx.
5) Dashboard widgets showing sampled rate, drop rate, and per-backend success rate and latency.
milestones: Spike: prototype binary with simple sampling and routing - done
Design review: config API and failure modes - done
Prototype perf run: 200k spans/s simulated - in progress
QA: e2e tests with Jaeger/Tempo - planned
design_decisions:
1) Stateless controller: avoid local durable queues, rely on short retry/backpressure and downstream buffering.
2) Sampling: prefer head-based sampling with optional tail-sampling hook placeholder for future work.
3) Health checks: backend selection based on weighted success rate over a 60s window; temporarily route to fallback if error rate > 1%.
4) Normalization: convert common attribute keys (service.name, http.route) to our canonical naming, and attach tenant_id header for Tempo ingestion.
5) Language/runtime: Go for low-latency gRPC handling and existing OTLP SDK interoperability.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: introducing a middle hop increases p99 latency. Mitigation: microbenchmarks and a feature flag to bypass controller in emergencies.
Risk: sampling misconfiguration causing customer data loss. Mitigation: default to conservative sampling (sample more) and a dry-run mode that tags but does not drop spans.
Risk: backend misrouting during partial outage. Mitigation: rapid failover rules + alerting and a circuit-breaker with exponential backoff.
test_plan: Unit tests for sampling logic, integration tests against local Jaeger and Tempo test containers, stress test with k6-style trace generator to validate 250k spans/s for short bursts, and canary e2e in prod-staging with synthetic traffic. Include regression test that ensures header mappings are preserved for trace search.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy to staging with config set to dry-run sampling for 48h.
2) Canary: enable routing for 1% of traffic in prod-observe-cluster for 24h with extra tracing.
3) Gradually increase to 25% then 100% over 72h while monitoring p99 latency and error rates.
4) If failure, flip bypass flag to send traffic directly to existing exporters.
5) Post-rollout review and tuning in next sprint.
observability_requirements: Expose Prometheus metrics: controller_ingest_total, controller_forward_success_total{backend}, controller_forward_errors_total{backend}, controller_sampled_total, controller_dropped_total, controller_processing_latency_seconds_bucket. Provide Grafana dashboard panels for p50/p95/p99 processing latency, sample rate by tenant, and per-backend success ratio. Create alerts for forward_error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m and processing_p99 > 100ms.
